Question B-006-001-003.

Why the correct answer is right: Cutting a uniform transmission line shorter does not change its conductor geometry or dielectric, so a 52-ohm line remains a 52-ohm line. The shorter piece has less length-dependent loss, not a different characteristic impedance.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "26 ohms": This wrongly scales impedance in direct proportion to the remaining length: 52 x (10 / 20) = 26. Characteristic impedance does not halve when the cable length is halved.
- sourceIndex 2: "104 ohms": This wrongly doubles 52 ohms as though removing half the cable doubled the line impedance. The geometry of the remaining piece is unchanged.
- sourceIndex 3: "13 ohms": This is 52 x (10 / 20)^2 = 13, a squared length-scaling error. Cable length is not used that way for characteristic impedance.
